text: Medium Working for 10 years within 5, and how you can ruin your mental health: | by cuteheart | Sep, 2026 | Medium Sitemap Open in app Sign up Sign in Medium Logo Get app Write Search Sign up Sign in cuteheart CuteHeart Technology Group & Exosystems | NSRI Lead Researcher Film Product Management Mental Health Philosophy Art Working for 10 years within 5, and how you can ruin your mental health: Dive in to the latest way to exploit your creative mind and become a slave to the maniacal big company terror cuteheart 8 min read · 1 hour ago -- Listen Share Press enter or click to view image in full size It’s served as a beautiful testbed and even helped me with my work in Film. As a compositor, I feel like I have a lot to thank garry’s mod for. Expressions, arithmetic, and calculus style regression are a product of my learning through the game and not from working on movies. Instead of positioning myself as the superstar who managed to set everything up, I would see myself cleaning up after them to get things to a graphical or visual fidelity that matches the rest of the show. The “eye” is a so called training of ones perception to see things that are not normal. You can develope a “eye” in just about anything, and it will translate to other things. Hairdressers know more about color than most Film editors, because they work with real pigments. I chose this example because the same exact lexical wording is used to describe both Hair and Video Games. Every part of working in movies is split in to pieces by the parts that make it expensive, and minimal staff is kept to bridge these key gaps. Discipline is learned from work and not directly teachable because of the nuance required to fill hats in two departments. In such a tight environment, every single minute is counted against the budget and every day becomes a write off. This is because visual effects companies do not pocket their pay until the work is finished, and until then a LOT of subsidizing is being done by a studio just to keep afloat. It’s a open secret that one show will be used to pay another and the records will be fudged on a producer level. Because of how fragile projects in movies are, the security attached to them allows for way more leniency in reporting than traditional accounts payable and receivables. What does that mean for the workforce? HR does not know how good you are, your lead doesn’t even know how good you are because of this speedy approach. This allows studios to fudge skill as “learning curve”. Some went as far as to create fake designation for those that were considered essential. In the movie world, essential means you are footing the bill if you don’t make it work. Coming from a environment where you had minutes for feedback able to make your entire week be stressful is a kind of environment that not a lot of people get to experience. Someone who has been through film understands the grind, but even then- being someone higher up the ladder begins turning to a question of balance. Film in its current form does not allow for work life balance, someone has to give. Someone has to be underpaid, whether its 20 people in India being paid 10% of what it takes to do 1 persons job, or if you are asked to take over work. At all times it’s capacity, and flushing that capacity. Your work stops being reviewed by supervisors, because you become technically more skilled and the glue turns to a talking head rather than real skills. The pipeline I was in was coarse but industrially standardized across all places that I worked at. Concept -> Previz -> PreComp/Layout -> Modeling/Rigging -> Animation/Texture -> Lighting -> Compositing Three of these steps happen simoultaneusly as two artists will take up the split. When you are someone in the pipeline, you only know as much as you need to and not as much as you should. Should means money, most people are scared of being paid more and fair enough. Higher pay makes a job more volatile to the results, but it does not invalidate the experience. Each of these stages happen in constant phases, because each single shot is prepared this way, everything that doesn’t need your eyes was cut at concept stage. If any sort of real footage comes in, then this becomes a new dimension to the entire workflow. 3D generated images, using computers (CGI) is at the behest of the person up the chain, and anyone higher up the chain has no idea whats going down beside one level lower. Concept artists don’t need to know what compositing or layout is, they need to provide previz with the mockups required to turn the previz to something that can be refined. Every step here is filtered, and if you mistake this to be a factory, you’re not wrong but you’re not right either. When you are closer to a concept, you work closer with the people who run the show. This not only secures the ideas but it also trickles down nuance setup from the get go. It becomes sacrisant to deviate unless permissible by the client. Clients are not rational, they don’t care about your feelings, your jobs, your employees or your ideas. I’ve watched someone get fired and rehired within 5 minutes, obviously after that they made Clients not sit with the artists — but the story holds. People who shot a movie don’t want to go through it’s visual effects to create the final piece they want to see everything live. That’s why you get live concerts, that’s why you get 4D movie theatres, and that’s why you got visually impressive AI. Pull it all back, and you start seeing a culture that doesn’t leave room for improvement, and anyone who is smart enough to wear those extra hats usually becomes wary of the conditions themselves. Rarely does someone score a job in a place for life, I am willing to bet that’s the exception more often than not. Movies are single companies during the time they are shot, edited and put together.
